chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who carried his slave upon an animal, so it trampled a man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fine is upon his master'.
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the fine if a slave carried on an animal tramples someone?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on animal liability, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the master bears the *ghurm* (compensation) when his slave, while being carried on an animal, causes injury to a third party. This ruling highlights the principle of vicarious liability in Shia jurisprudence, where the owner is responsible for the actions of those under his control, distinguishing it from cases where the animal itself is the direct cause of damage.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who carried his slave upon an animal, so it trampled a man. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The fine is upon his master’.
